    meta:

}

arguments.summary: A spear-phishing campaign attributed to APT-41 (Double Dragon) successfully compromised a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042) via malicious Outlook macro execution. The initial payload, identified as a ShadowPad variant, established C2 communication over HTTPS to a known-bad IP (198.51.100.23) and performed host file modification to enable persistence. Lateral movement was attempted via SMB to a file server (10.0.3.10), and credential access attempts were observed. Despite detection by IDS and EDR systems, containment actions (firewall block, user disable, endpoint isolation) were not executed due to approval workflow failures. The endpoint AV scan returned no findings, indicating evasion capabilities.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dll_IndirectSyscalls {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike beacon DLL using indirect syscalls and common strings"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        malpedia_reference = "https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.cobalt_strike_beacon"
        malpedia_version = "20260409"
        malpedia_license = "Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal"
    strings:
        $s1 = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT" wide ascii
        $s2 = "GET / HTTP/1.1" wide ascii
        $indirect_call = { FF /5 } // Call [reg] pattern for indirect syscall
        $config_marker = { 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 } // Common beacon config padding
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and // MZ header
        #s1 > 1 and #s2 and $indirect_call and $config_marker
}
